name: CapCut Chapter Card Slide Interrupt
use_when: A tutorial, essay, countdown, or tips video needs a clean section reset.
The viewer benefits from a full-screen pattern interrupt instead of another small text overlay.
The background and title can be designed consistently enough to become a reusable series style.
avoid_when: The segment is too short for a full-screen card and the card would slow pacing.
The card repeats captions or says something the speaker already made clear.
The background has low contrast, dated styling, or mismatched brand colors.
The transition would hide the first useful words of the next section.

timeline_pattern.pattern: end_of_spoken_section -> background_card_overlay_slide_in -> title_text_entrance -> brief_read_hold -> text_out -> card_slide_out -> return_to_footage
timeline_pattern.pattern_interrupt_rule: Use the card as a scene change, not merely extra text on top of stale footage.
timeline_pattern.background_rule: Use a project-owned color, gradient, or simple designed background that keeps text high contrast.
timeline_pattern.text_rule: Keep the card copy short, such as tip number, chapter name, or outcome phrase.
timeline_pattern.exit_rule: Animate both text and background out before the body footage resumes.

motion.rule: Background and text motion should feel deliberate and simple: slide, zoom, or fade, then settle quickly for reading.

keyframe_values.canvas_size: Design source backgrounds at the project delivery ratio, such as 1920x1080 for horizontal or 1080x1920 for vertical.
keyframe_values.background_in: Slide in from the side or use a clean wipe only when it fits the style.
keyframe_values.text_in: Use a restrained zoom or fade; avoid delaying the title.
keyframe_values.read_hold: Hold long enough to read the chapter label before returning to footage.

sound.rule: A small whoosh, tick, or hit can mark the card entrance if it does not cover the speaker's next line.

captions.rule: Suppress ordinary captions during the card if the card text carries the spoken words; restore captions when talking-head footage returns.

color.rule: Use background colors or gradients that fit the series palette and keep the title readable at phone size.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use a generated color/gradient or imported background, draw short title text, animate overlay x/y or alpha, and trim tightly to the section reset.
implementation.remotion: Create a ChapterCard component with backgroundAsset, title, subtitle, inAnimation, outAnimation, durationFrames, and captionSuppression fields.
implementation.blender: Use a 2D card plane, text objects, and simple camera/opacity motion for more stylized section cards.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create or import a designed background, add it as an overlay, fit full screen, add a simple slide-in animation, add short title text with a restrained zoom/fade, then animate both out before returning to footage.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Color Matte/gradient/image background plus Essential Graphics text, Motion keyframes or presets, and caption suppression during the card.

common_mistakes: Using a full-screen card when a small label would be faster.
Choosing a low-contrast or dated background that makes the edit feel less premium.
Leaving captions duplicated under the chapter card text.
Letting the card animation cover the next spoken section.
Changing card colors/fonts randomly instead of building a reusable series grammar.
qc: Does the card mark a real section reset or pattern interrupt?
Is the chapter/title readable at phone size?
Do text and background animate out before the next body beat?
Are duplicate captions suppressed during the card?
Does the card style match the project's reusable visual identity?
